# Proverbs 13 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 13:3 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | One-guarding his-mouth keeps his-soul; one-opening-wide his-lips — destruction for-him. |
| LOGOS | Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life; he who opens wide his lips comes to ruin. |
| PNEUMA | Watch your words and you protect your life. Talk without thinking, and you'll destroy yourself. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 13:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Craving but-there-is-not — [the]-soul-of [the]-sluggard; but-[the]-soul-of [the]-diligent is-made-fat. |
| LOGOS | The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing, while the soul of the diligent is richly supplied. |
| PNEUMA | A lazy person wants everything but gets nothing. A hard worker gets everything they need and more. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 13:7 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | There-is one-making-himself-rich and-there-is-nothing at-all; one-making-himself-poor and-wealth [is] great. |
| LOGOS | One pretends to be rich, yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth. |
| PNEUMA | Some people pretend to be rich but have nothing; others pretend to be poor but are actually wealthy. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 13:8 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Ransom-of a-man's life [is] his-riches, but-a-poor-man does-not-hear rebuke. |
| LOGOS | The ransom of a man's life is his wealth, but a poor man hears no threat. |
| PNEUMA | A rich person's wealth can buy their way out of danger, but a poor person never even hears a ransom demand. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| LOGOS | The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be put out. |
| PNEUMA | The life of a righteous person shines brightly, but the wicked person's lamp will be snuffed out. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
